detail.longDescription: Hi HN, I'm Rafael. Europe Instead is a directory of European-made software: https://europeinstead.com I built it because every time we needed a new tool at my startup, Upgrid, I ended up doing the same research again: who actually owns this company, where is the data hosted, who are the subprocessors. After doing that enough times I got tired of it and started writing it down properly. The existing "EU alternatives" lists didn't help much, because most check one thing, the legal seat. A company registered in Berlin can be owned by a US parent, run on AWS us-east-1, and send your data to a dozen US subprocessors. That is a different risk from a Berlin company on Hetzner. So every tool gets two separate answers: - Origin score (0-100): how European the company is, from five parts: legal entity, ownership and control, operations, data residency, and openness. Weights are published on the method page. - Exposure level (1-5): which jurisdictions can legally reach the core customer data, based on where it is hosted and who the subprocessors are. Every fact links to the page it came from, with the check date and usually a quoted line. If we couldn't find evidence, the fact is shown as "not verified" and scores zero, rather than being guessed. Right now that is about a quarter of all facts, which tells you something about how little vendors disclose. Some details: - 1,818 tools from 33 countries, across 212 categories, mapped as alternatives to 453 US products (Calendly, Typeform, Intercom, Google Analytics, and so on). - Vendors can correct their record by form or email. Corrections are reviewed by a person and logged in a public change history. - Listing is free and unconditional. No backlink required, and rankings can't be bought. If I ever sell sponsored slots, they sit above the ranked list with their own numbering and a "Sponsored" label; the ranking below always starts at 1 and doesn't move. A few things you might find useful: - "Alternative to X" pages: name the tool you use today and see the European ones that do the same job. - Stacks: a full European set of tools for a small company, one per job. - A read-only API and an MCP server, so you can ask an AI assistant for a European alternative and get the sourced record back ( https://europeinstead.com/developers ). - A free badge vendors can embed. It links to their live record and has no tracking. What I'd like from you: tell me where the data is wrong, and tell me where the method is wrong. In particular I'm unsure how to treat the UK and Switzerland (included, country always shown so you can apply a stricter definition), and whether "uses AWS Frankfurt" should count against a tool as much as it does now.
